chunks: And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan from Najjah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Mu'tamir (one performing Umrah al-Mufradah) enters Mecca, if he is not a Mutamatti', then after he performs Tawaf around the House, and Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, and prays the two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), let him return to his family if he wishes.
And he said: 'The Umrah al-Mufradah and the Umrah al-Mut'ah were revealed because the Umrah al-Mut'ah entered into the Hajj, but the Umrah al-Mufradah did not enter into the Hajj.'

So it is not contradictory to what we have presented, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'and the Umrah al-Mufradah did not enter into the Hajj' means the Umrah that is performed in the months other than the months of Hajj.
Because the Umrah al-Mufradah only enters into the Hajj if it occurs in the months of Hajj.
And whenever the matter is as we mentioned, then it is not sufficient in place of the Umrah al-Mut'ah.
And that which confirms what we have presented.

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and part of Shawwal)
key_terms.التَّمَتُّعِ: Tamattu', a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined
key_terms.الْعُمْرَةُ الْمُفْرَدَةُ: Independent Umrah, performed separately from Hajj
key_terms.الْمُتَعَةُ: Umrah al-Mut'ah, Umrah combined with Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Umrah al-Mufradah and Umrah al-Mut'ah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) to clarify the jurisprudential nuance that Umrah al-Mufradah only integrates into Hajj when performed within the sacred months, distinguishing it from Umrah al-Mut'ah which is inherently linked to the Hajj season. This distinction underscores the Shia view that the two forms serve different ritual purposes, with the independent Umrah not automatically satisfying the Tamattu' requirement unless specific temporal conditions are met. The hadith thus reinforces the structural separation of these rites in Shia fiqh, emphasizing that the legal status of Umrah depends heavily on its timing relative to the Hajj months.
